clue.text: Gets worried about a single layer in the archaeological site

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters sit around the other pieces
worried means the letters of gets are agitated into a new order

parts.note: a single thing is one
a hen is a bird that lays eggs, a layer

explanation.surface: Someone fretting over one stratum found at a dig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' and 'about' are the anagram and wrapping signals. 'layer' looks like a stratum at the dig, but here it is a bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The great prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain is England's best-known ancient monument.

clue.text: Keats's lake-side plant, southern boundary

parts.note: an edge is a boundary

explanation.surface: A botanical note on a poet's waterside reed marking the southern limit.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats wrote 'The sedge has withered from the lake' in La Belle Dame sans Merci.
explanation.definitionFit: This grassy waterside plant is named in the opening stanza of a Keats ballad.

clue.text: Pass mark

parts.note: read not as an exam threshold but as going past a target

explanation.definitionFit: To go beyond the intended point or target is to fail by excess.

clue.text: Issue the French find embarrassing

parts.note: issue means offspring, so this is a child that the French would call terrible, in their own words

explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for a shocking, unconventional person who embarrasses their own circle.

clue.text: Banqueting without a starter so far towards the rising sun

definitions.text: so far towards the rising sun

indicators.note: a starter is a first course, so the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: banqueting is feasting

explanation.surface: Diners who skipped the first course at a dinner in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: An easting is a distance travelled east, towards sunrise; 'starter' plays on the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: In navigation and map grids it is the distance measured eastward from a reference line.

clue.text: He has gold in liquid measure, a W African resident

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a gill is a quarter-pint liquid measure
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A man holding gold in a small glass, an African local.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold; a GILL is a small British liquid measure, a quarter of a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: This great ape lives in the forests of western and central Africa.

clue.text: This test to find a champion?

parts.note: El Cid, the Spanish hero, was called the Campeador, the champion

explanation.surface: A trial meant to identify the best competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: El Cid's title Campeador means champion; the acid test is the decisive proof, once used to tell gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase acid test names a decisive trial, from nitric acid used on gold.

clue.text: Singers could become rich nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means the zero is placed inside the rearranged letters
could become signals that the letters of rich turn into another arrangement

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A poor man musing that he might get wealthy from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' rearranges RICH to CHIR, and 'in it' sets O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of people who sing together, often in church.

clue.text: Price demanded by Diana for sack

parts.note: Di is short for Diana; with 'by' it is read possessively, Di's
a charge is a price demanded

explanation.surface: A princess's fee for firing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Something demanded by Diana is Di's, giving the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an employee from a job is to fire them.

clue.text: A potential bloomer taking them over the herring-pond?

definitions.text: A potential bloomer taking them over the herring-pond?

parts.words: A potential bloomer taking them over the herring-pond?
parts.note: the bloomer is a flower, the Mayflower, the ship that carried these settlers across the herring-pond, a jocular name for the Atlantic

explanation.definitionFit: These English settlers sailed to Plymouth, Massachusetts in 1620 on the Mayflower.

clue.text: Alfred whose accusers Emile accused

parts.note: Emile Zola's open letter J'accuse attacked those who framed a French army officer named Alfred

explanation.definitionFit: The French Jewish captain wrongly convicted of treason in 1894, defended by Zola.

clue.text: One in our sun's explosion causing disaster

indicators.note: in means the single letter goes inside the scrambled letters
an explosion blows the letters of our sun apart into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A solar explosion that wrecks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' rearranges OURSUN, and 'in' puts I inside to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calamitous brings destruction or financial ruin.

clue.text: Do we have to have this oil?

definitions.text: Do we have to have this oil?

parts.words: Do we have to have this oil?
parts.note: something we have to have is indispensable, and the same word names the aromatic oil distilled from plants

explanation.definitionFit: It means indispensable, and it also describes a volatile aromatic plant oil.

clue.text: Old garden but no house for painter William

indicators.note: but no means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: William Hogarth was the 18th-century English painter

explanation.surface: An artist without a home of his own is left with only a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth painted A Rake's Progress; HO is the dictionary abbreviation for house.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or dialect word for an enclosed yard or garden, as in a cloister garth.

clue.text: Way-out drink

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eccentric beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way-out' looks like one word meaning weird; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong dark beer brewed with roasted malt.

clue.text: I can still put in order this bright spark

indicators.note: put in order says the letters of I can still are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone claiming they can still organise things, a clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny trace or spark, from the Latin word for a spark.

clue.text: Old circus performer very happy breaking up a riot

parts.note: glad means happy

indicators.note: breaking up signals that the letters of a riot are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A delighted entertainer stopping a riot at the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' rearranges ARIOT to IATOR. The circus is the Roman arena, not the big top.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained fighter who battled in the arenas of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Sort of steel vestment used by Galileo

indicators.note: sort of signals that the letters of steel are sorted into a different order

parts.note: a cope is a long cloak-like church vestment

explanation.surface: A metal church garment supposedly worn by the astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo built and turned an optical instrument for magnifying distant objects on the night sky.

clue.text: How to get weaving in treacle manufacture

indicators.note: manufacture means the letters of in treacle are made into something new

explanation.surface: A method for producing woven goods from syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross threads over and under one another, as in a woven fabric.

clue.text: A soft sort of pudding to act as a sop

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
pease pudding is a British dish of boiled split peas

explanation.surface: Offering a gentle pudding to placate someone.
explanation.walkthrough: PEASE pudding is a British dish of mashed boiled split peas.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify someone by giving in to their demands, as a sop does.

clue.text: Roscius after retirement becomes tax-collector?

parts.note: a retired person is an ex-, a former one
Quintus Roscius was the most celebrated actor of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A famous Roman performer taking a new job collecting taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Roscius was a famous Roman actor; once retired he is a former actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who demands payment or extorts money, such as a collector of levies.

clue.text: "What, frighted with — fire?" (Hamlet)

parts.note: the missing word is from Hamlet's taunt when the king flees the play, referring to the stage gunfire that was only pretend

explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet mocks the king for being scared by sham, untrue fire in the play scene.

clue.text: Musical passage associated with Italian fruits?

explanation.definitionFit: It is a passage played by all the performers together, and it is the first half of tutti-frutti, an ice cream with mixed fruits.

clue.text: Augustus's successor's opening the Rome-Ostia link

indicators.note: the opening of the name is its first part, so the ending is dropped

parts.note: Tiberius succeeded Augustus as Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An emperor inaugurating the road between Rome and its port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like a ribbon-cutting but means the start of TIBERIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flows through Rome to the sea at Ostia, linking city and port.

clue.text: Works in a profession in search of perfection?

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor or lawyer carries on their profession, and one rehearses repeatedly because practice makes perfect.

clue.text: Reveal secret of Adriatic resort

explanation.definitionFit: To inform on someone is to give away a confidence, and the Croatian port on the Dalmatian coast bears the same name.

clue.text: Found in bed when a bit of ear trouble returns

parts.note: the lobe is the soft lower part of the ear

indicators.note: returns says the word for trouble is turned back to front

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Earache coming back while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns AIL to LIA. 'bed' is a flower bed, not one to lie in.
explanation.definitionFit: A low bedding plant with small blue flowers, grown in garden borders.

clue.text: Whistle-stop operator put in work in the plant

indicators.note: put in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: toil is work
a referee stops play with a whistle

explanation.surface: A train driver at a small station assigned to a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: A whistle-stop is a small station, but here the referee blows the whistle to stop play.
explanation.definitionFit: A clover-like plant with three-part leaves.

clue.text: That subtle air a high-class academy gives us

parts.note: U means upper-class in British usage
RA is the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: An elite school bestowing a refined atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: U means upper-class, from 1950s British social commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive atmosphere or emanation that seems to surround a person or place.

clue.text: In which Lot's wife was turned to salt

definitions.text: In which Lot's wife was turned to salt

parts.words: In which Lot's wife was turned to salt
parts.note: in Genesis Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and became a pillar of salt; this is the act of looking back

explanation.definitionFit: Looking back over past events, as Lot's wife fatally did.
